gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-thai-loo: Noto Sans Thai Looped stands tall, its lowercase looking almost bold. Origami answers with one brush stroke of constant width, and that unwavering hand against such generous gaps at the curve ends is the pair's best trick.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Noto Sans Tifinagh is all rounded, open shapes, like inflated bowls filling the line. Noto Sans Tifinagh keeps a long stretch of text inviting and easy on the eye, while Origami's lettering stays single-stroke and flat beside it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Origami draws every stroke, diagonals included, with the same heft as its stems, like a sign-painter's brush. Noto Sans Tirhuta, with its dominant x-height, makes the strongest partner.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Approachable and compact, with hardly any step between lowercase and capitals, this body reads like an open chalk arc. Noto Sans Ugaritic sits next to Origami's monoweight strokes and its poured-lead lowercase, and the two feel like friendly neighbors.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai makes words look like solid blocks rather than skylines. Noto Sans Vai keeps that steady, generous space around its curves, so a longer stretch reads smoothly beneath Origami's cable-like strokes.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Modern in feel, Noto Sans Vithkuqi opens up its a, c, e and s and barely steps from capital to lowercase. And over a long passage that openness keeps going, a quiet foil to Origami's pipe-cleaner letterforms.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho is hulking, its lowercase like thick chalk pressed hard. Origami does the unshaded, never-swelling line best, while Noto Sans Wancho does the heavy, wide-mouthed lowercase.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-warang-c: Contemporary through and through, Origami draws with a marker-nib line that ignores direction. Noto Sans Warang Citi handles the rest, building words into solid blocks with wide channels leading into each counter.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-yi: Modern and businesslike, Noto Sans Yi gives its lowercase a deep midsection and rounds left unlatched like a hook. Origami's brush line never swells, and that gap is the draw.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-zanabaza: Approachable and tall, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square soars with its x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. And a longer read stays comfortable, with Origami's no-thick-no-thin strokes handling the display work above.
